headline: South Asia: PM Shehbaz, CDF Munir share top spot in list of world’s 500 most influential Muslims
script:
Good morning. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: PM Shehbaz, CDF Munir share top spot in list of world’s 500 most influential Muslims.
- Asia: Could Beijing’s HQ-17 air-defence system defend PLA amphibious forces from Taiwan strikes?.
- Western Russia: Romanian PM condemns Russian attack on three commercial vessels in Black Sea.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
United States - bottom line: US Air Force adopts new Force Design focusing on sensors and autonomy.
- Military Times, 2 days ago: US Air Force adopts new Force Design focusing on sensors and autonomy.
The Air Force's new Force Design 2026 outlines a shift toward artificial intelligence, autonomy and integrated sensors to counter emerging threats.
The Caribbean - bottom line: We’ve broken the glass ceiling, but have we overcome? – Luz Longsworth.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 11 hours ago: We’ve broken the glass ceiling, but have we overcome? – Luz Longsworth.
WESTERN BUREAU: Women have shattered glass ceilings, claimed executive offices, and risen to the highest levels of leadership. But Dr Luz Longsworth is challenging the notion that reaching the top means the battle is won. “We have broken a lot of ceilings, but we have not overcome,” the veteran academic and corporate leader declared last Wednesday evening, warning that women’s growing presence in powerful positions should not be mistaken for the disappearance of barriers to their success. “Don’t let our firsts be our lasts,” she urged.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

SOUTH AMERICA
South America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

EUROPE
Western Russia - bottom line: Romanian PM condemns Russian attack on three commercial vessels in Black Sea.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 3 hours ago: Romanian PM condemns Russian attack on three commercial vessels in Black Sea.
Romanian PM Luca Niculescu has warned of worsening Black Sea security caused by Russia's war against Ukraine following drone strikes on vessels, including the Greek-flagged tanker Evia Petrol V near the Danube Delta.
- The Moscow Times, 5 hours ago: At Least 1 Killed as Ukraine Strikes Industrial Sites Across Russia.
Ukraine’s military claimed responsibility for strikes in Tatarstan, saying it had targeted the Nizhnekamskneftekhim petrochemical complex.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 3 hours ago: Russians strike Odesa, damaging civilian infrastructure.
Odesa authorities have confirmed that civilian infrastructure across the region – including grain warehouses and a car dealership in Odesa – was destroyed in fires caused by a Russian attack on 15 November.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 5 hours ago: Ukraine's General Staff also reports strike on Akhtubinsk airfield in Russia and drone launch site.
Ukraine's General Staff says a strike on Russia's Akhtubinsk airfield caused a secondary detonation at a missile kit depot, and a drone launch site in Oryol Oblast was hit.
Southern Europe - bottom line: Romania slams ‘unacceptable’ drone strikes on Black Sea ships.
- Politico Europe, 4 hours ago: Romania slams ‘unacceptable’ drone strikes on Black Sea ships.
Three commercial vessels were hit near Romania’s coast, prompting fighter jet deployments and fresh calls for NATO support to strengthen Black Sea security.
- Politico Europe, 14 hours ago: Ukraine claims thousands of Russian casualties and a slowing Kremlin advance.
Ukraine is countering Russia's narrative of battlefield success by blunting the Kremlin's attacks.

AFRICA
Persian Gulf Region - bottom line: Iran targets US military radar in Bahrain in ‘retaliatory’ drone strikes.
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, 5 hours ago: Iran targets US military radar in Bahrain in ‘retaliatory’ drone strikes.
Iran’s IRGC says six drones were launched at a US radar installation at an air base in Bahrain.
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, 4 hours ago: Explosive attack targets investigative journalist’s home in Panama.
An investigative journalist’s home in Panama was attacked in a suspected bombing.
- Jerusalem Post, 8 hours ago: Ukraine moving toward Israeli-Italian satellite terminals instead of Starlink - report.
Though unconfirmed, the move would provide Ukrainian operators an alternative communications channel for drones
- Jerusalem Post, just now: Hamas commander targeted at Nasser Hospital loses leg, suffers severe head injury.
Israeli sources say Hamas's Khan Yunis commander survived the Nasser Hospital strike but suffered severe head injuries and had his leg amputated.
Africa - bottom line: Daily life in Sudan paralysed by deepening fuel crisis and rising costs.
- Africanews, 2 hours ago: Daily life in Sudan paralysed by deepening fuel crisis and rising costs.
Domestic refining has been crippled by the civil war while the Middle East conflict has led to significant fluctuations in oil prices.
- Africanews, 10 hours ago: DR Congo: Ebola-awareness campaigns conducted at schools in Bunia.
About 40 schools in the province have reported cases of Ebola since classes resumed in September, with one teacher dying of the disease.
South Africa: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: PM Shehbaz, CDF Munir share top spot in list of world’s 500 most influential Muslims.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 6 hours ago: PM Shehbaz, CDF Munir share top spot in list of world’s 500 most influential Muslims.
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir have shared the top spot in the latest edition of the world’s 500 most influential Muslims, alongside the Saudi king and crown prince and the Turkish president. The rankings have been compiled by the Royal Islamic Strategic Studies Centre (RISSC), a research institute based in Amman, Jordan. It has been publishing an annual report titled “The 500 Most Influential Muslims” since 2009, recognising and highlighting individuals who have made significant contributions to Muslim communities.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 6 hours ago: Blasts rattle Bahrain as Iran launches second drone attack in 3 days.
Blasts echoed over Bahrain on Sunday as the tiny Gulf nation was rattled by the second Iranian drone attack in three days, ending a long lull in strikes during the Middle East war. Sirens rang out, and authorities posted several alerts on social media urging residents to seek shelter, their first warnings since September. Iran’s Revolutionary Guards said they carried out a drone attack on a US radar system in the desert island state, which hosts US military facilities including a major naval base.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 23 hours ago: Major among 4 troops martyred, 24 terrorists killed during operations in KP and Balochistan: ISPR.
Four troops, including a major, were martyred while 24 terrorists were killed in multiple intelligence-based operations (IBOs) in Balochistan and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s North Waziristan, the military’s media wing said on Saturday. In a statement, Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said that since Nov 13, armed forces have been conducting multiple IBOs “around Kolpur, Kardagap and Nushki, including area domination and patrolling of the Quetta-Taftan National Highway (N-40) to keep it secure for local traffic and sustain operations”.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 3 hours ago: Gatherings in KP's Bajaur, Lakki Marwat, Swabi, Tank banned for 30 days.
BAJAUR/LAKKI MARWAT/SWABI: The district administrations of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Bajaur, Lakki Marwat, Swabi and Tank on Sunday imposed Section 144 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC) for a month, banning public gatherings and several other activities amid the prevailing law and order situation. In Bajaur, the district administration prohibited all kinds of political gatherings, “hate speech” against the state and the display of arms and weapons for 30 days.
Asia - bottom line: Could Beijing’s HQ-17 air-defence system defend PLA amphibious forces from Taiwan strikes?.
- South China Morning Post - China, 13 hours ago: Could Beijing’s HQ-17 air-defence system defend PLA amphibious forces from Taiwan strikes?.
Before mainland Chinese troops could attempt a landing on Taiwan, they would first have to assemble vehicles, weapons and supplies along the coast – potentially exposing them to Taiwanese drone, rocket and missile attacks. A nighttime drill reported by state broadcaster CCTV on June 11 offered a glimpse of how the People’s Liberation Army could shield those amphibious forces as they prepared to cross the Taiwan Strait. - South China Morning Post - China, Politico Europe, 5 hours ago: Top Hamas commander killed in Israeli strike in Gaza.
Hamas said on Sunday that a senior commander who helped plan and oversee the October 7, 2023, attack on Israel had been killed in an Israeli air strike, with the Israeli ‌military confirming his death. Samir Abu Younis, 53, the commander of the Rafah brigade, was killed on Saturday, said the Palestinian militant group’s armed wing, the Al-Qassam Brigades. The Israeli military said it had killed Abu Younis in a strike in the southern Gaza Strip overnight, ⁠adding that he had led the Rafah brigade...
- South China Morning Post - China, 4 hours ago: Chinese J-10C fighter spotted carrying modified Russian-origin heavy-strike missile.
New state media footage has surfaced showing for the first time what appears to be a Chinese-modified variant of the Russian-origin Kh-29T air-to-surface missile mounted on a J-10C fighter jet. State broadcaster CCTV’s social media account posted a video on Wednesday featuring Chinese fighters, showing the missile mounted under the 4.5-generation fighter as it took off, according to posts by Chinese military bloggers over the weekend. China originally imported about 2,000 Kh-29T missiles...
- South China Morning Post - China, Ukrainska Pravda, Jerusalem Post, Politico Europe, just now: Estonia to close Russia border after ‘sabotage’ bid, foreign minister says.
Estonia said on Sunday it would close its border with Russia after stopping what it said was an attempted arson attack by Russia’s GRU military intelligence on a drone factory. “Estonia will close all Estonian-Russian border crossing points as of 1 December,” Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna posted on social media, citing “clear evidence” that the GRU had ordered the attack. Earlier on Sunday, Prime Minister Kristen Michal wrote on social media that the GRU had ordered a “sabotage attempt” at the...
India - bottom line: "If US Makes Another Mistake...": Top Iran Negotiator Warns Trump.
- NDTV - Top Stories, 8 hours ago: "If US Makes Another Mistake...": Top Iran Negotiator Warns Trump.
Donald Trump has alternated between threats of escalating the Iran war with a fresh attack and winding down hostilities.
- NDTV - Top Stories, 9 hours ago: 12 Killed, 16 Injured As Bus With Gas Refinery Employees Overturns In Iran.
Authorities have warned the death count could rise due to the severity of some of the injuries, the report said.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 2 hours ago: J&K terror attack: Search operation launched to hunt terrorists who attacked CRPF post.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 3 hours ago: Pakistan orders 1 lakh Turkish FPV drones, expands unmanned warfare arsenal.
Korean Peninsula - bottom line: Son Heung-min laments unrewarded effort against Saudi Arabia after 3-2 loss.
- Yonhap News Agency, 2 days ago: Son Heung-min laments unrewarded effort against Saudi Arabia after 3-2 loss.
AL RAYYAN, Qatar, Nov. 13 (Yonhap) -- South Korea captain Son Heung-min said Fri...

AUSTRALIA
Australia - bottom line: Jordan sentences three men to death over deadly church attack.
- ABC News Australia, South China Morning Post - China, The Hindu - International, 5 hours ago: Jordan sentences three men to death over deadly church attack.
An Israeli air strike has killed a senior Hamas military commander in Khan Younis in southern Gaza, Israel says, while Jordan dishes out death sentences after last month's attack in the city of Karak.
- The Guardian - Australia, 11 hours ago: Anthony Albanese welcomes Trump-Xi-Putin summit – even as European leaders express reservations.
‘We think dialogue is a good thing,’ Australian PM says after German chancellor urges the US to work with Europe for peace in Ukraine Australia has endorsed this week’s historic summit between Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin in China, even as European leaders warn that the US president must not make major concessions over the war in Ukraine. The three-way summit is planned to take place in Shenzhen, where the leaders will gather for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) meeting.
- The Guardian - Australia, 3 hours ago: Gender-diverse Australian sailors barred from US submarines despite Aukus deal, documents reveal.
Defence briefing released under freedom of information laws shows ADF beholden to US directives when in training Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast Aukus is effectively forcing the Australian navy to comply with a US ban on transgender people in the military with gender-diverse navy recruits prevented from starting a career in nuclear submarines because they would not be safe training on US boats.
- The Guardian - Australia, 3 hours ago: How sensitive data from Centrelink and other Australian agencies may have been fed to Palantir software.
Exclusive: Personal information of Centrelink clients and childcare workers is among data shared with ACIC, which uses US tech company’s software The personal information of Centrelink customers, taxpayers and childcare workers is among a trove of sensitive data that may be ending up in Palantir’s surveillance software in Australia, without the departments responsible for the information even knowing about it.
